summary: BrokerOS Phase 1 Extension (Case Notes Timeline + PDF Invoice Generation) tested end-to-end. Backend: 38/38 pytest tests pass (11 new tests added for notes timeline and invoice PDF). Frontend: All UI flows for adding notes (with char counter, teal author, grey timestamp) and downloading PDF invoices (filename INV-YYYY-NNNN.pdf with success toast) verified working.

minor.issue: Length enforced server-side, but error returns 400 with English message - consider returning 422 to match Pydantic validation convention (currently uses manual HTTPException). Not blocking.
Invoice sequence increments per request even on retries/failed downloads - sequence numbers can have gaps. Acceptable per spec but worth documenting.

issues: Counter '17 / 2000' shows but no visual warning (red color) when approaching/exceeding 2000 chars - 'Add Note' button still appears clickable on >2000 input until backend rejects

action_items: (Optional) Add red counter color when noteContent.length > 2000 and visibly disable Add Note button at client side beyond limit
(Optional) Return 422 instead of 400 for >2000-char note (consistent with Pydantic validation)
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1147 lines - growing further past the 700-line guideline. Strongly recommend splitting into routers/ (auth, clients, cases, lenders, commissions, notes, invoices, documents, dashboard).

generate_invoice_pdf is a synchronous reportlab routine invoked inside an async endpoint - blocks the event loop for the duration of PDF generation. For low-load preview this is fine, but consider running in a threadpool (asyncio.to_thread) at scale.

Invoice sequence write is not transactional (find_one then update_one). Under concurrent invoice generation by the same user, two requests could compute the same next_num. Use $inc with findOneAndUpdate(upsert=True) atomically.
Note content length validated twice (Pydantic model + manual check). Pydantic max_length=2000 on NoteCreate.content yields 422; manual check is redundant - keep one.
POST /api/notes / invoice endpoints correctly pop _id after insert - no ObjectId leak (regression check passed).
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (added TestNotesTimeline class with 7 tests and TestInvoicePDF class with 4 tests)
seed_data_creation: Pytest creates TEST_-prefixed clients/cases/lenders/commissions/notes and cleans up at end via test_zzz_cleanup. UI test added 1 note ('TEST UI note ...') to the seed case 09ecdc6c-828e-4134-b316-9c112ccd2848 - left in DB intentionally for inspection. Invoice sequence for admin user incremented to 5 during testing (INV-2026-0001 through INV-2026-0005 generated).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 1 extension fully working. Backend test suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py now has 38 tests including notes timeline (7) and invoice PDF (4). Invoice endpoint returns PDF with X-Invoice-Number header and Content-Disposition filename INV-YYYY-NNNN.pdf. Frontend CaseDetail uses data-testid: case-notes-section, notes-count, note-textarea, note-char-count, add-note-btn, notes-list, note-author-<id>, note-time-<id>. Commissions page uses generate-invoice-<id>. Toast on success: 'Invoice <number> downloaded'. Note: invoice sequence has incremented to 5 - tests that check absolute numbers should not assume starting at 0001.
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs found in Phase 1 extension. Implementation is correct: notes are immutable, sorted desc by created_at, author derived from logged-in user's first_name+last_name with email fallback; invoice PDF uses reportlab, sequence stored in invoice_sequences collection keyed by user_id with current_year tracking, returns StreamingResponse with X-Invoice-Number header consumed by frontend to set download filename.
